references.text: 2. Exodus 12 describes the origin and institution of Passover as an annual festival for the Jews.
2. Chronicles 35 documents King Josiah's celebration of Passover, which is the most detailed description of how the festival was observed in the Old Testament, directly linked to the term 'Passover'.
Ezra 6:19-22 tells of the returned exiles who celebrated Passover and uses the same terms for the festival ('Passover') that are central in John 6:4.
John 11:55-56 also describes the situation just before Passover in Jerusalem, where people were seeking Jesus, using identical context regarding the proximity of the festival.
John 12:1 begins with the time reference 'six days before Passover', which is a direct chronological and thematic link to the time reference in John 6:4.
